cases.title: $each repeats an array item once per element, splicing in order
$as names the binding; $index, $first and $last are available
$if keeps an item when truthy and drops it when not, and is removed from the output
With both, $each runs first and $if filters each element
$each works on any array, here a table's rows
$each over an empty array leaves no item
cases.notes: Present and empty is not absent: no error.

cases.title: $if on an absent optional variable drops the item, without an error
cases.notes: fancy-expr's rule: an absent path is null, and null is falsy. A TOKEN reading an absent variable fails (resolve 0009); a CONDITION asking whether it is there must not.

cases.title: $each over an absent optional array is TEMPLATE_MISSING
cases.notes: Rendering nothing would be the silent-empty outcome the plan refuses. A template that may have no rows says so with `$if: "people"` on a wrapper.

cases.title: Directive keys are removed wherever they were written; other keys keep their order
$each inside a paragraph's runs
A separator with `$if: "!$first"`
cases.notes: The simple case; 0012 is the separator.

cases.title: Nested arrays let an element carry its own separator run
cases.notes: $first is the INNERMOST loop's, and an inner array item with only $if is not a loop, so it reads the outer one.

cases.title: $each takes a dotted path
In nested loops, $index is the innermost loop's
$if sees the loop binding and the declared variables together
A $value splice is replaced in place by one rendered copy of $value per element
cases.notes: The splice exists because a holy-sheet row is an ARRAY and a directive sits only on an object, so before it a row could not repeat. The splice object itself is not output.

cases.title: $value may be any JSON value: 0, false and null are copied, not treated as missing
cases.notes: Catches an implementation that tests `$value` for truthiness or uses an isset-style check: null is a value here (an empty cell).

cases.title: A splice over an empty array produces nothing
cases.notes: Present and empty is not absent: no error, as for $each (0006).

cases.title: $if on a splice is evaluated once per element, as with $each
$value and $if written before $each behave exactly as written after it
cases.notes: JSON key order is not something an author should have to get right (SPEC 8). Catches an inspector that only creates the binding when it reaches $each.

cases.title: $value may be an object: the splice then behaves like an object $each
cases.notes: The same output as 0001, written the other way. The object is matched by the element's path, blocks.*, so its runs are text fields.

cases.title: $value may contain directives: a splice inside a splice, inner $index winning
cases.notes: SPEC 8 decision: arrays inside $value take directive elements and splices like any other array, under the same limits.directiveDepth (limits 0028/0029).

cases.title: A splice over an absent optional array is TEMPLATE_MISSING at its $each
cases.notes: As for $each (0008): rendering nothing would be the silent-empty outcome.

cases.title: An error inside a spliced value is reported at its template path, through $value
cases.notes: A JSON Pointer into the TEMPLATE (SPEC 6), never an index into the expanded output: the second copy fails, and its path is the one cell the author wrote.
